summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease, polycystic kidney disease, and refractory atrial fibrillation was admitted with fever, hypotension, and dyspnea following a recent discharge. She developed pneumonia, confirmed by chest imaging, and was treated with antibiotics. Due to persistent tachycardia and intolerance to rate-control medications, she underwent a successful modified AV ablation. She was started on digoxin for rate control and discharged home in stable condition. Her liver enzymes were elevated during admission, likely due to antibiotics, and require outpatient follow-up. She resumed her dialysis schedule and was advised to monitor weight and continue anticoagulation.
